article_title: Underpinnings of the Costs of Flexibility in Preschool Children: The Roles of Inhibition and Working Memory
citation: Chevalier N., Sheffield T. D., Nelson J. M., Clark C. A. C., Wiebe S. A., Espy K. A. (2012). Underpinnings of the Costs of Flexibility in Preschool Children: The Roles of Inhibition and Working Memory. Developmental Neuropsychology. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC3308575/
title: Go/No-Go and Nebraska Barnyard tasks measuring inhibition and working memory in preschoolers
description: The Go/No-Go task, adapted from Simpson and Riggs, presents fish (Go, 75% of trials) and sharks (No-Go, 25%) with children pressing a button for fish and withholding for sharks; the percentage of correct No-Go responses indexes "inhibition of the prepotent, more frequent button press response." The Nebraska Barnyard is a computerized complex span task adapted from the Noisy Book in which children remember sequences of animal names and press corresponding colored boxes, with span scored as "the maximum span length (highest span where the subject was correct on two trials)." Both were standardized before entering multilevel models so their effects on costs were directly comparable.
requirements: Standardization of scores prior to modeling to allow direct comparison of inhibition and working-memory effect magnitudes
Discontinuation criteria in the span task to manage young children's fatigue and noncompliance
target_learning_goals: assessing inhibitory control and working-memory maintenance in early childhood
examples: Children completed 40 Go/No-Go test trials (30 Go, 10 No-Go) and span trials beginning at sequences of two animals
